data.value: AV1 and VP8 are not offered: on an ordinary phone they have no hardware encoder, and encoding them in software costs far more than they give back.

data.name: CheckUsbDriverMissing
data.value: A device is plugged in but Windows has no driver for it; on a phone, that is its debugging interface. 1. Download Google's USB driver from developer.android.com/studio/run/win-usb and unzip it. 2. Device Manager › right-click the line with the yellow triangle › Update driver › Browse my computer › Let me pick from a list › Have Disk › the folder's android_winusb.inf file › "Android ADB Interface". Windows asks for administrator rights and may warn the driver does not look made for the device: confirm. 3. Unplug and replug the cable.

data.name: CheckUsbOther

data.name: CableHelpTitle
data.value: A plugged-in device Windows cannot read

data.name: CableHelpIntro
data.value: The phone may well be charging, which only proves power. The data wires carry nothing usable. Here are the leads, from the most common to the rarest.

data.name: CableHelpSteps
data.value:
Try another cable. Many cables shipped with a charger have no data wires, and a damaged data cable gives exactly this fault.
Try a USB 2.0 port, at the back of the machine rather than the front: enumeration is more forgiving there and the path is shorter.
Restart, do not shut down. With Windows fast startup, shutting down and powering back on does not reinitialise the USB controllers; only "Restart" does.
Clean the phone's connector. Pocket dust keeps the data pins from making contact while charging still works.
Cross the tests: another device on this port, and this phone on another PC. You will then know which of the three is at fault.

data.name: AdbShellUserAccessDenied
data.value: The phone refused the PC access to that profile. If it is a secure folder, unlock it on the phone before launching. Otherwise turn on “USB debugging (security settings)” in the developer options.

data.name: ScrcpyDisplayTimeoutWithAudio
data.value: The phone did not open a virtual display in time. Try without sound first: on some tablets, turning it on is enough to stop the display from opening.

data.name: BrandSamsungWarning
data.value: If “USB debugging” is greyed out with “Blocked by Auto Blocker”, or the device is not detected at all, turn off “Auto Blocker” in Settings > Security and privacy, then “Block USB connections” in the other security settings. A secure folder has to be unlocked before launching, or the game will not be found in it.

data.name: BrandOnePlusWarning
data.value: Also turn on “USB debugging (security settings)” and “Install via USB” in the same menu. Without the first one the picture shows but the mouse and keyboard do nothing.

data.name: BrandVivoWarning
data.value: Also turn on “USB debugging (security settings)” and “Install via USB” in the same menu. Without the first one the picture shows but the mouse and keyboard do nothing.

data.name: DeadInputExplanation
data.value: The picture shows, the window opens, and yet clicks and keystrokes do nothing. No error appears, because there is none: the device agrees to show its screen, but not to receive your gestures. That is a separate permission, and it is granted on the phone.

data.name: DeadInputTestHelp
data.value: The check asks the device to accept an input event, using the key Android calls “unknown”, which triggers nothing anywhere. It says in one second what otherwise takes an evening to find out.

data.name: DeadInputTestWorks
data.value: The device accepts input simulation. If clicks still do nothing, the cause is below, not here.

data.name: DeadInputTestDenied
data.value: The device refuses input simulation. That is the cause: turn on the setting below, then run the check again.

data.name: DeadInputTestUnknown
data.value: No verdict. The device answered something unexpected, and guessing would be worse than saying nothing.

data.name: DeadInputTestNoDevice
data.value: No device connected. Plug one in or pair it, then run the check again.

data.name: DeadInputSecurityHelp
data.value: In the developer options, turn on the line whose description reads “Grant permissions and simulate input via USB debugging”. Depending on the brand it is called “USB debugging (security settings)”. This is by far the most common cause.

data.name: DeadInputCable
data.value: The cable has to carry data

data.name: DeadInputCableHelp
data.value: When the phone asks for the connection mode, pick “File transfer”, not “Charging”. A cable left on charging lets the screen show while refusing everything else. If the question never appears, try another cable: many cables shipped with a charger have no data wires.

data.name: SimulatedKeyboardTip

data.name: SimulatedKeyboardHelp
data.value: Turn this on when the window answers the mouse but nothing you type appears: the on-screen keyboard of some brands swallows the characters. In exchange, the phone reads your keys through its own Android layout, so set that layout to match your PC keyboard, or an AZERTY will type as QWERTY.

data.name: DeadInputRevokeHelp
data.value: In the developer options, press “Revoke USB debugging authorisations”, unplug the device, plug it back in, and accept the prompt again. It clears an authorisation left half granted, and it is the step that unblocks the cases where everything looks correctly set.

data.name: DeadInputToggleDeveloper
data.value: Turn it all off, restart, turn it all back on

data.name: DeadInputToggleDeveloperHelp
data.value: Unplug the phone from the PC first. Then turn off the debugging switches, up to three depending on the brand: USB debugging, install via USB, and USB debugging (security settings). Restart the phone, turn them back on once it has restarted, then plug it back in on “File transfer” and accept the prompt. The order matters, and so does the restart: turning them back on without it often leaves the setting ticked without being applied.

data.name: WindowFreezes
data.value: A window freezes after a while

data.name: SleepExplanation
data.value: DT Hub keeps active the virtual screen the game runs on, but Android puts to sleep by itself the applications it judges idle, and a game window that is not in the foreground is one of them. The windows then freeze one after another, the oldest first. One setting is enough to prevent it, and it holds.

data.name: RemoveRestrictionsHelp
data.value: The game must be able to run in the background without limit. This is the only handling needed in most cases, and it survives restarts.

data.name: RepeatForEachCopy

data.name: RepeatForEachCopyHelp
data.value: A cloned application, or one installed in a second profile, is a separate application in Android's eyes: it has its own restrictions, and the setting made on one does not hold for the other.

data.name: AlreadyFrozenHelp

data.name: HelpFixCableWire
data.value: • Try another cable: many only charge.

data.name: HelpFixCableMode
data.value: • In the phone's USB notification, try “File transfer”.

data.name: HelpFixCableRevoke
data.value: • Developer options: “Revoke USB debugging authorisations”, then plug it back in.

data.name: HelpFixCableWindows
data.value: • Windows does not see the phone? The Devices tab says what to do.

data.name: HelpFixWifiRestart
data.value: • After a restart, turn “Wireless debugging” back on: the pairing is kept.

data.name: BrandSamsungFixCable
data.value: • Samsung: turn off “Auto Blocker” (Settings › Security and privacy), then “Block USB connections”: they hide the phone from the PC.

data.name: BrandHonorFixCable
data.value: • Honor, Huawei: also turn on “Allow ADB debugging in charge only mode” in the developer options, if your version offers it.

data.name: BrandHonorFixWifi
data.value: • Honor, Huawei: without Google services, wireless debugging is sometimes missing. Use the cable then.

data.name: HelpFixCableUnlock
data.value: • Unlock the phone: the request only shows on an unlocked screen.

data.name: HelpFixWifiScreen
data.value: • To pair, keep the code screen open on the phone: it only shows itself to the PC meanwhile.
